purpose: Teach: 初対面/待たさ/ヘッドホン/トレイ/興味津々/へっ/はぎ/通り過ぎる

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.jp: 葵、お客様、お友達と初対面でも楽しそうにお話されてたよ、メイちゃん
lines.en: Aoi, that customer was chatting away so happily with her friend, even though they'd only just met.
lines.style: Soft, unhurried observation; gentle wonder rising on the first-meeting part.

lines.speaker: aoi_barista
lines.jp: 葵、お客様、混雑で長く待たされたけど笑顔だったよ、メイちゃん
lines.en: Mei, one customer got kept waiting forever in the rush, but she never stopped smiling.
lines.style: Warm, melodic, a touch rueful about the rush; brightening on the smile.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.jp: 葵、お客様、店内BGMをヘッドホンで聴き直されてたよ、メイちゃん
lines.en: Aoi, that customer was listening back to the café's playlist on her headphones.
lines.style: Quiet amusement, hushed as if sharing a small secret across the counter.

lines.speaker: aoi_barista
lines.jp: 葵、お客様、お盆、つまりトレイの色合いをお褒め下さったよ、メイちゃん
lines.en: Mei, a customer complimented the coloring of our obon — the trays, I mean.
lines.style: Pleased, lilting delivery; the tiny self-correction handled with an audible smile.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.jp: 葵、お客様、新しいメニューに興味津々で質問されてたよ、メイちゃん
lines.en: Aoi, that customer was so intrigued by the new menu — she had a question about everything.
lines.style: Gentle enthusiasm on the customer's behalf; pace lifting through the flood of questions.

lines.speaker: aoi_barista
lines.jp: 葵、お客様、「へっ、それくらいなら朝飯前さ」って笑ってらしたよ、メイちゃん
lines.en: Mei, one customer laughed, "Heh, that much? Piece of cake!"
lines.style: Playful imitation of the customer's gruff boast, then a warm chuckle right after.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.jp: 葵、お客様、秋の花のはぎ、つまり萩を眺めに来店されたって、メイちゃん
lines.en: Aoi, that customer said she came in just to admire the hagi — the autumn bush clover.
lines.style: Slow, tender delivery; lingering on the flower's name as if picturing the blossoms.

lines.speaker: aoi_barista
lines.jp: 葵、お客様、お店の前を通り過ぎる人波を眺めてらしたよ、メイちゃん
lines.en: Mei, one customer just sat there watching the stream of people passing by out front.
lines.style: Soft winding-down close; slow pace, gaze drifting toward the window with the words.
